lesson_title: The Lazy Plunger and the Instant One
hook_text: Two syringes, one tube. Fill with air and the far plunger is lazy. Fill with water and it moves before you blink.
clip_script: Join two syringes with a tube. Fill them with air and push. The far plunger hesitates, then creeps out late, and when you press on it the whole thing feels like a pillow. Now fill them under water so there is not a single bubble, and push. The far plunger jumps out the same instant, the same distance, and pushes straight back on your thumb. Air squashes. Water does not. Swap in a syringe twice as big and push the small one. The big plunger moves half as far but you can hold it against double the force. Push the big one and the small plunger flies out twice as far with half the force. No lever anywhere, just the size of the plunger faces. That is why the rescue device uses water, why it is filled under the surface, and why the syringe you push should be smaller than the one that drives the jaws if you want a grip.
visual_style: Whiteboard pair of syringes and a tube; ghosted plunger showing the lag with air, crisp arrow with water; then unequal syringes with distance marks 4 and 2.
mood: Hands-on discovery, the surprise of the lazy plunger made sense of.
pacing: Two quick demonstrations, then the unequal pair, then three design conclusions in one breath.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and run the four syringe tests yourself with a results table.
